proposals: DGCI&S should publish an official 8-digit concordance mapping every retired or split code to its successor codes, with the year each change took effect, replacing the bare asterisk, so the 31.8 per cent of export value and about 39 per cent of import value on new codes can be linked to their history.

DGCI&S should report the unit of quantity for each code year by year in TradeStat and flag any change of unit, so a switch such as crude petroleum moving from tonnes to kilogrammes under an unchanged KGS label cannot silently break unit-value series.

The Department of Commerce should give TradeStat stable, linkable report URLs and annual bulk downloads at the 8-digit level, including country-wise data, so users need not copy codes into a POST-only form to find where a product is exported.

DGCI&S should fill the FY2021-22 gap in the commodity-wise export series on TradeStat, or publish a note explaining its absence, so comparisons across that year are not forced to treat a two-year change as an annual one.
